page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-compute ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled, requiring the attachment of remote block volumes, and no discrete GPUs are present. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution alongside steady multi-core compute capability. The instance achieved top-quartile performance in single-core workloads, registering 3058.98 on stress-ng and 2067.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, with notable efficiency in text processing (2644.0). Multi-core processing aligns with mid-tier expectations for an 8-vCPU slice, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 8087.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14386.29. In memory benchmarks, small cached blocks reached 603.65 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read throughput declined to 35.48 GB/sec. Operational tests showed 11.3 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 12.29 GB/sec in static web serving.

Due to its high RAM allocation relative to vCPU count, this configuration offers solid cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise tasks that do not require massive parallel core scaling. It is well-aligned with in-memory caching layers, medium relational databases, ETL batch transformations, and Java or Python backend services, while large-scale LLM inference is constrained by CPU execution speeds.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-64 is a memory-dense compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 physical cores, 8 dedicated vCPUs, and 64.0 GB of RAM, offering an elevated ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local NVMe storage and no GPU hardware, relying on external network storage for persistent disk capacity. In benchmark testing, the platform shows strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2067.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3058.98, while multi-threaded throughput and Redis operations place in the median tier. With 64 GB of memory paired with 8 dedicated execution threads, this profile suits memory-heavy workloads, in-memory data caching, relational database hosting, and general backend application serving.
